l4_steps.name: Generate parts demand forecast from maintenance programme
l4_steps.input: Approved maintenance programme, fleet utilisation plan, AD/SB list
l4_steps.output: 12-month rolling parts demand forecast by P/N
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥85% (MAPE ≤15%)
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet mix changes (737 MAX vs 737-800 intermix) cause demand volatility; AMOS forecast module requires manual adjustment for new-type introductions where consumption history is sparse

l4_steps.name: Validate forecast against consumption history and ADs
l4_steps.input: 24-month parts consumption history, current AD/SB revision delta
l4_steps.output: Validated demand plan with confidence bands; exception list for manual override
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast review cycle completed within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Sporadic demand items (rotables with <4 removals/year) produce unreliable AMOS statistical forecasts; manual override requires SME judgement and is not auditable within AMOS

l4_steps.name: Submit demand plan to procurement and finance for budget approval
l4_steps.input: Validated demand plan, prior-year actuals
l4_steps.output: Approved materials budget, MRP requirements released to procurement
l4_steps.kpi: Budget approval lead time ≤10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: No native AMOS–SAP interface at many carriers; demand plan must be manually re-keyed into SAP MRP, introducing transcription errors and plan drift between systems

l4_steps.name: Check stock availability against net demand requirements
l4_steps.input: Approved demand plan, real-time inventory snapshot
l4_steps.output: Net requirements list with buy / borrow / exchange decisions per P/N
l4_steps.kpi: Stock-out rate ≤2% for critical AOG-flagged parts
l4_steps.pain_point: Inventory accuracy degrades when technicians issue parts without closing work orders in AMOS; phantom stock causes missed AOG events and emergency buys that erode savings from planned procurement

l4_steps.name: Source parts from approved vendor list via RFQ
l4_steps.input: Net requirements list, approved vendor master, contract pricing
l4_steps.output: RFQ issued to ≥2 approved suppliers per part number
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor lead time compliance ≥90%; RFQ issued within 1 business day of requirement
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA/EASA Part 145 approved supplier list is slow to update; unapproved parts risk is highest on spot-market buys where non-qualified vendors are used to satisfy urgent demand

l4_steps.name: Evaluate supplier quotes and select preferred source
l4_steps.input: Supplier quotes, cost and lead-time matrix, AOG flag
l4_steps.output: Awarded PO, supplier selection rationale documented
l4_steps.kpi: PO cycle time ≤3 business days (AOG: ≤4 hours)
l4_steps.pain_point: AOG situations force bypass of normal sourcing controls; expedited buys from non-preferred vendors increase counterfeit-part risk and undermine FAR Part 145 traceability requirements

l4_steps.name: Issue purchase order and confirm supplier delivery commitment
l4_steps.input: Awarded quote, budget confirmation, delivery address
l4_steps.output: PO issued with confirmed expected receipt date and freight tracking reference
l4_steps.kpi: PO-to-delivery on-time rate ≥88%
l4_steps.pain_point: International freight delays for OEM parts (Boeing, CFM International); post-2022 supply chain disruption continues to affect lead times for 737 MAX-specific components, inflating AOG exposure

l4_steps.name: Receive parts shipment and verify airworthiness documentation
l4_steps.input: Inbound shipment, packing list, FAA 8130-3 or EASA Form 1
l4_steps.output: Goods receipt logged in AMOS; documents scanned and attached to part record
l4_steps.kpi: Receiving processing time ≤4 hours for AOG-flagged parts; ≤24 hours for routine receipts
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete or missing FAA 8130-3 / EASA Form 1 is common on spot-market purchases; quarantine and supplier chase delays average 3–5 days, directly extending AOG events

l4_steps.name: Inspect parts for airworthiness and serviceable condition
l4_steps.input: Physical part, airworthiness release certificate, inspection checklist
l4_steps.output: Inspection record; pass/fail determination recorded against part in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Inspection turn-time ≤8 hours; incoming rejection rate ≤3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Counterfeit parts detection requires detailed visual and dimensional checks; AMOS quality module lacks integration with industry counterfeit databases (IATA TACT, EASA SACA) forcing manual cross-reference

l4_steps.name: Quarantine non-conforming parts and raise supplier NCR
l4_steps.input: Failed inspection record, non-conformance details
l4_steps.output: Quarantine tag applied, Non-Conformance Report raised, supplier notified
l4_steps.kpi: NCR resolution cycle ≤15 business days; quarantined parts segregated within 1 hour of rejection
l4_steps.pain_point: Quarantine storage space is constrained at line stations; disposal of life-limited parts requires documented destruction to prevent re-entry into supply chain per FAA Order 8120.11

l4_steps.name: Assign bin location and update AMOS inventory record
l4_steps.input: Accepted and inspected part, warehouse bin map
l4_steps.output: Part binned, inventory record updated with location, quantity, and batch traceability
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory location accuracy ≥99.5%; bin assignment completed within 2 hours of acceptance
l4_steps.pain_point: Barcode label degradation in hangar environments (heat, hydraulic fluid) causes scan failures and phantom inventory; manual overrides bypass AMOS audit trail, creating traceability gaps

l4_steps.name: Monitor shelf-life, expiry dates, and life-limited part counters
l4_steps.input: Part life data, calendar expiry dates, flight-cycle counters from OEM CMM
l4_steps.output: Expiry alerts actioned; scrapping orders raised for time-expired or cycle-expired parts
l4_steps.kpi: Shelf-life compliance 100%; zero expired parts issued from serviceable stock
l4_steps.pain_point: Elastomeric seals and composite consumables have 12–24 month shelf lives; AMOS expiry alerts require manual acknowledgement — risk of expired parts being issued if alert is dismissed without action

l4_steps.name: Conduct periodic cycle counts and reconcile inventory discrepancies
l4_steps.input: Cycle count schedule, physical count results, AMOS on-hand quantities
l4_steps.output: Reconciled inventory record; adjustment or write-off requests submitted to Finance
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory accuracy post-count ≥99%; cycle count variance ≤1% by value
l4_steps.pain_point: High-velocity consumables (O-rings, safety wire, lockwire) are difficult to count accurately; inventory write-offs require Finance (SAP FI) approval causing multi-day delays before AMOS quantities are corrected

l4_steps.name: Receive and validate parts request from maintenance work order
l4_steps.input: Work order task card, illustrated parts catalogue reference, parts list
l4_steps.output: Validated picking list generated in AMOS; estimated staging time confirmed to technician
l4_steps.kpi: Parts picking initiated within 30 minutes of WO request submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Late parts requests from technicians (defects discovered mid-task) disrupt shop flow; AMOS WO-to-stores interface requires sub-task closure before parts issuance, slowing technician access during time-critical events

l4_steps.name: Kit and stage parts at work centre before task start
l4_steps.input: Validated picking list, bin locations, task start time
l4_steps.output: Kitted parts trolley staged at work centre; all P/Ns and quantities verified
l4_steps.kpi: Kitting accuracy ≥99%; kit staged ≥1 hour before scheduled task start
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute P/N substitutions (alternate part approved for use) require a Quality Inspector re-verification before issuance; kitting errors discovered at point-of-use cause unplanned AOG delays averaging 2–4 hours

l4_steps.name: Issue parts to technician and record WO consumption in AMOS
l4_steps.input: Kitted parts, technician badge and signature, work order number
l4_steps.output: Parts issued; WO consumption record updated; removed serviceable/unserviceable parts tagged and returned to stores
l4_steps.kpi: Parts issuance documentation completeness 100%; removed parts tagged within 1 hour of removal
l4_steps.pain_point: Technicians informally borrowing parts without AMOS issuance record causes inventory inaccuracy and traceability failures — a regulatory non-compliance risk under FAR Part 43 and EASA Part 145.A.42

l4_steps.name: Tag and track removed unserviceable rotable in AMOS
l4_steps.input: Removed component, completed work order removal record
l4_steps.output: Unserviceable tag applied; unit status set to U/S in AMOS rotable tracking module with part history appended
l4_steps.kpi: Rotable U/S tagging compliance 100%; AMOS update completed within 4 hours of removal
l4_steps.pain_point: Missing part histories on purchased used rotables from secondary market; AMOS rotable module requires manual re-entry of pre-purchase records from prior operators, with no standardised data exchange format

l4_steps.name: Assess repair viability against BER threshold
l4_steps.input: Unserviceable rotable, OEM Component Maintenance Manual, preliminary repair cost estimate
l4_steps.output: Repair or BER decision documented; repair order raised in AMOS or scrapping order approved
l4_steps.kpi: BER rate ≤8% of annual rotable pool; average repair cost vs. new-unit cost ≤60%
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM shop visit pricing (especially CFM International LEAP engine components) is non-transparent and has risen >25% since 2022 due to supply shortages; BER thresholds require quarterly recalibration to remain accurate

l4_steps.name: Ship core to approved repair agency and track shop visit TAT
l4_steps.input: Raised repair order, serviceable-to-repair shipping documentation, export/import permits
l4_steps.output: Core shipped with AMOS shop visit opened; TAT clock started; interim exchange unit sourced if required
l4_steps.kpi: Repair TAT ≤30 days for avionics LRUs; ≤60 days for engine accessory components
l4_steps.pain_point: Third-party MRO shop visit visibility is limited; AMOS shop visit module does not receive real-time status feeds from external MRO providers — manual status chasing required, with average 10-day response lag inflating fleet-level rotable pool size

l4_steps.name: Receive repaired rotable and return to serviceable stock
l4_steps.input: Repaired unit, MRO shop work order, EASA Form 1 or FAA 8130-3, updated part history
l4_steps.output: Rotable returned to serviceable stock in AMOS; shop visit closed; cost posted to SAP asset record
l4_steps.kpi: Rotable pool availability rate ≥92%; receiving and return-to-stock processing ≤4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Repaired units occasionally returned at a different modification standard or with higher-than-quoted cost; configuration mismatch requires re-inspection and potential work-order revision, delaying return to pool by 1–3 days
